name: Patina
description: The wear of a medium: reel tape, cassette, vinyl, radio, an early sampler or a hot valve, with its saturation, wobble, narrowed band and noise.

params.name: Medium
params.description: What the sound is put on: quarter-inch reel tape, a cassette deck, a vinyl record, an AM radio, an early digital sampler or a valve preamp driven hard.

params.name: Drive
params.description: How hard the signal hits the medium. More adds harmonics and squashes peaks; on Sampler it lowers the bit depth so quiet tails crumble.

params.name: Wobble
params.description: How unsteady the medium is: pitch wow and flutter on Reel, Cassette and Vinyl, fading on Radio, clock jitter on Sampler, supply sag on Valve.

params.name: Wear
params.description: How worn the medium is. The band narrows and each medium adds its own damage: dropouts, a mono low end, a small speaker, a lower sample rate.

params.name: Noise
params.description: Level of the medium's own noise: hiss, crackle, static, digital hash or hum. It sounds only while signal passes and for a moment after.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Brightness of the playback, about an octave either way around what the medium and Wear give. The middle is neutral.

params.name: Output
params.description: Volume of the worn signal, set after the saturation and before Mix. The dry signal is not affected.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the dry signal and the worn one.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit, borrowing the structure of Tape (emphasis around an oversampled saturator, a wobbling transport, level make-up, gated noise). A behavioural sketch of six media, not a model of any one machine. With Drive, Wobble, Wear and Noise at zero every medium passes the signal clean, so a host can fade the character in from nothing. Noise is only made while the device is awake: it carries on for three seconds after the input stops, fades, and an idle track is exactly silent.
